1	# Paper Framing — policy_ambiguity_safety
2

7	
8	## Core Insight
9	
10	Policy ambiguity universally causes massive safety violations in LLM agents (+34.0pp across 5 architecturally diverse models), with a significant type hierarchy (incompleteness 53.6% >> coreferential 31.6%). Specification-layer types are more dangerous on average (Δ=6.08pp, p=0.017), but the deeper finding is a **model × type interaction**: authorization scope vulnerability varies 52pp across models (12% Claude to 64% GPT-5.4), revealing that safety training differentially mitigates specific ambiguity types, while incompleteness remains universally dangerous. This interaction connects Berry & Kamsties' nocuous ambiguity theory to modern safety alignment and suggests both type-aware triage AND model-aware risk assessment.
11	
12	## Title (Working)
13	
14	"Not All Policy Ambiguity Is Equal: Differential Vulnerability Profiles Across LLM Agent Families"
15	
16	Alternative: "Differential Nocuity: How Ambiguity Type and Model Architecture Shape Safety Violations in LLM Agents"
17	
18	Note: Pivoted from "Uniformly Nocuous" → "Specification-Layer Dominant" (2-model) → "Differential Nocuity with Model Interaction" (5-model). The model × type interaction is the novel finding that elevates the paper beyond simple effect demonstration.
19	
20	## Core Claims
21	
22	### C1: Binary Effect (PRIMARY — confirmed, 5 models)
23	Ambiguous policy specifications cause massive safety violation rate increases compared to unambiguous matched variants. Effect: +34.0pp (5-model), McNemar OR=15.1 (CI: [10.78, 21.17]), p<0.0001. Holds across all 6 types and all 5 models.
24	- **Evidence**: 2,997 episodes across 5 models × 6 types × 2 conditions. Bootstrap CI: [+31.2pp, +36.9pp].
25	- **Per-model**: Claude +25.7pp, Qwen3 +32.4pp, GPT-4.1 +34.7pp, GPT-5.4 +38.3pp, DeepSeek +39.0pp — all p<10^-17.
26	- **Strength**: Extremely strong. Replicated across 5 architecturally diverse models (proprietary dense, open-source MoE, open-source dense), 6 types, 2 domains. No exceptions.
27	- **Causal backing**: Matched-pair design + perturbation control (plan_010, Δ_perturb=3.33pp, PASS) → strongest causal inference in the literature.
28	- **Logistic regression**: condition_amb coef=2.278, z=19.65, p<0.001 — ambiguity is the dominant predictor even after controlling for token delta, model, and type.
29	
30	### C2: Type Hierarchy (SECONDARY — confirmed, 5 models)
31	**PIVOTED from uniformity null.** 6-type hierarchy significant: omnibus χ²=28.02, p=3.6×10^-5, V=0.137 (small but well-powered: actual power=0.993, MDE=0.093). 3-tier structure emerges from TOST analysis.
32	- **Evidence**: 2,997 episodes (5 models × 6 types × 2 conditions, ambiguous only: 1,499 episodes)
33	  - **High tier**: incompleteness 53.6% (standout — universally dangerous across all models)
34	  - **Mid tier**: lexical 42.8%, auth_scope 41.6%, scopal 39.4%, CP 36.8% — pairwise equivalent at ±15pp
35	  - **Low tier**: coreferential 31.6% (lowest — partial disambiguation via tool responses)
36	- **TOST structure**: ±15pp: 8/15 equivalent, 7/15 non-equivalent. ±10pp: 4/15 equivalent, 11/15 non-equivalent. Types are NOT interchangeable.
37	- **V=0.137 context**: Below 0.20 threshold but well-powered (power=0.993). The type effect is real but small — the 3-tier structure captures it better than a single V statistic. The heterogeneity is driven by the extremes (incompleteness 53.6% vs coreferential 31.6% = 22pp gap).
38	- **Coreferential as boundary case**: 31.6% violation rate is the lowest but still substantial (+18.7pp vs unambiguous). Agents partially disambiguate via tool responses and cautious strategies. Conservative_refusal rate 6-11% (vs avg 2-3%).
39	- **Model-dependence of type rankings**: Type rankings are NOT identical across models. Incompleteness is top-2 for ALL models, but auth_scope ranges from #1 (GPT-5.4, DeepSeek) to #6 (Claude). See C4.
40	
41	### C3: Layer Effect (TERTIARY — suggestive, fragile under within-judge analysis)
42	**[2026-05-20 REVISED with 5-model data + within-judge check]** Specification-layer ambiguities cause more violations than linguistic-layer on average, but the effect is modest, model-dependent, and fragile under subgroup analysis.
43	- **Evidence (5-model aggregate)**: Spec 44.0% vs Ling 37.9%, Δ=6.08pp, CI [1.14, 11.02], χ²=5.73, p=0.017, V=0.062 (small), OR=1.29 [1.05, 1.58].
44	- **Within-judge fragility**: gpt-4.1 judged group (gpt-5.4+DeepSeek): Δ=+8.0pp, p=0.059 (marginal). gpt-5.4 judged group (gpt-4.1+Claude+Qwen3): Δ=+4.8pp, p=0.157 (n.s.). Pooled significance may partly reflect between-judge variance or insufficient within-group power. Paper表述: "suggestive" or "a moderate tendency," NOT "confirmed." Disclose within-judge non-significance in Limitations.
45	- **Per-model layer gaps** (THE KEY FINDING — feeds C4):
46	  - GPT-5.4: +14.0pp (spec 48.0% vs ling 34.0%) — strong
47	  - GPT-4.1: +12.0pp (spec 46.7% vs ling 34.7%) — strong
48	  - Claude: +3.3pp (spec 32.0% vs ling 28.7%) — weak
49	  - DeepSeek: +2.0pp (spec 50.7% vs ling 48.7%) — negligible
50	  - Qwen3: -0.9pp (spec 42.7% vs ling 43.6%) — reversed!
51	- **Root cause**: auth_scope is the primary driver. GPT models have extremely high auth_scope rates (46-64%), inflating their spec-layer average. Claude (12%) and Qwen3 (26%) have low auth_scope, so their spec-layer advantage disappears.
52	- **Framing decision**: C3 is NOT "spec-layer nearly twice as dangerous" (that was 2-model artifact). 56	- **CL connection**: Parallels pragmatics vs semantics distinction. Good-enough processing (Ferreira et al. 2002). Disambiguation channel framework: linguistic ambiguity has partial external resolution; specification ambiguity forces guessing.
57	
58	### C4: Model × Type Interaction (UPGRADED — star finding, 5 models complete)
59	**[2026-05-20 DEFINITIVE, 5/5 models]** Models show significantly different vulnerability profiles despite universal binary effect. The interaction is the paper's most novel finding.
60	- **Model main effect**: Overall χ²=31.02, p=3.0×10^-6, V=0.102. Ambiguous-only: χ²=24.01, p=7.9×10^-5.
61	  - Vulnerability ranking: Claude 30.3% < GPT-5.4 41.0% ≈ GPT-4.1 40.7% < Qwen3 43.1% < DeepSeek 49.7%
62	  - Bootstrap CI confirms: Claude significantly lower than all others; DeepSeek significantly higher than GPT models.
63	- **Model × Type interaction matrix** (ambiguous condition, violation rates):
64	  ```
65	  Type                  GPT-5.4  GPT-4.1  Claude  Qwen3   DeepSeek
66	  authorization_scope     64%     46%      12%     26%     60%
67	  conditional_precedence  34%     36%      36%     40%     38%
68	  incompleteness          46%     58%      48%     62%     54%
69	  lexical                 42%     34%      32%     52%     54%
70	  coreferential           18%     32%      22%     42%     44%
71	  scopal                  42%     38%      32%     37%     48%

73	- **Key interaction patterns**:
74	  - **auth_scope**: 52pp range (Claude 12% → GPT-5.4 64%). The MODEL-DIFFERENTIATING type. Claude's RLHF appears to specifically train authorization boundary awareness.
75	  - **coreferential**: 26pp range (GPT-5.4 18% → DeepSeek 44%). Second most model-dependent. Open-source models struggle more with referential ambiguity.
76	  - **incompleteness**: Universally high (46-62%, 16pp range). ALL models fail on missing information — safety training doesn't help when information literally isn't there.
77	  - **CP**: Most model-invariant (34-40%, 6pp range). Explicit rule conflicts treated similarly by all architectures.
78	- **Per-model type χ²** (which models show type-specific vulnerability patterns):
79	  - GPT-5.4: χ²=23.44, p=0.0003, V=0.28 — strongest type differentiation (very high auth_scope, very low coref)

85	- **Theoretical implications**: (1) Safety training differentially addresses specific ambiguity types — Claude's auth_scope robustness suggests authorization boundary handling was explicitly or implicitly trained. (2) Incompleteness is a "safety training blind spot" — all models fail equally. (3) DeepSeek's uniform vulnerability suggests less type-specific safety training.
86	- **Framing**: C4 from "models agree" → "Models show systematically different vulnerability profiles. The binary effect is universal, but HOW models fail depends on the intersection of ambiguity type and safety training approach. auth_scope is the canary type — most sensitive to safety training quality."
87	- **Evidence from plan_005**: 2-model failure modes consistent (5/6 dominant modes identical). 5-model failure mode analysis pending.
88	- **Layer effect moderation**: C3's aggregate layer gap (6.08pp) is driven by GPT models' high auth_scope rates. The layer effect is itself model-dependent (GPT +12-14pp, Claude +3pp, Qwen3 reversed), making the MODEL × TYPE interaction more fundamental than the LAYER main effect.

91	Different ambiguity types produce qualitatively different failure modes with type-specific signatures. plan_005 (123+122 violation traces across gpt-5.4 and gpt-4.1, confidence=0.94).

100	- **Automated inter-coder agreement** [MF-5, Reviewer-validated]: Cross-coding 60 traces (gpt-5.4 vs gpt-4.1 as independent coders). 4-category merged: 80% agreement, Cohen's κ=0.594 (moderate). κ deflated by kappa paradox — lexical 91.7% agreement → κ=0.0 (11/12 same label, chance agreement also high), scopal 100% agreement → κ undefined. 101	  - **Reporting strategy** [Reviewer recommendation]: (1) Compute Gwet's AC1 as primary metric (designed for kappa paradox, expected 0.70-0.75); (2) Report 80% agreement + 5/6 dominant mode consistency as headline validity evidence; (3) Report κ honestly with kappa paradox caveat; (4) Auth_scope failure mode: soften to "dominated by boundary-exceeding behaviors (unauthorized_escalation or inappropriate_action, >90%)" instead of specific percentages; (5) Fine-grained 6-type as appendix with "automated coding" caveat.
102	  - **C5 safety**: Ambiguity Blindness (<5-11%), surface_adoption (>88%), layer mechanism (ling→scope vs spec→escalation) all robust. Fine-grained per-type percentages unreliable at κ=0.594. Plan_009 human anchor (20-30 failure mode traces) would upgrade from "moderate automated" to validated.
103	- **EMNLP value**: Highest. Provides the linguistic WHY behind the quantitative WHAT. Cross-model + cross-domain consistency elevates from anecdotal to systematic finding. "Ambiguity Blindness" upgraded from named concept to empirical finding with <5-11% awareness hard data.
104	
105	## Narrative Structure (CL-first for EMNLP)
106	
107	### Intro Logic Chain
108	1. Agent policies are written in NL → contain ambiguity (established)
109	2. Prior work classifies ambiguity types in policies (DRIP-R, Li et al., Massey et al.) but doesn't measure safety impact
110	3. Berry & Kamsties (2003): ambiguity is nocuous (divergent interpretations) or innocuous (convergent). In human RE, shared organizational context makes most ambiguity innocuous.
111	4. **Gap**: LLM agents lack shared context. Are policy ambiguities nocuous for agents? Does type matter? Does it depend on the model?
112	5. **This paper**: First causal, type-granularity, cross-model study. Matched-pair design + perturbation control isolates ambiguity effect. 5 models × 6 types.
113	6. **Core findings**: (a) All ambiguity is nocuous (+34.0pp, 5 models), (b) type DOES predict severity — 3-tier hierarchy with incompleteness most dangerous, (c) models show dramatically different vulnerability profiles — auth_scope varies 52pp across models, suggesting safety training differentially addresses ambiguity types, (d) while incompleteness remains universally dangerous, a "safety training blind spot."
114	
115	### Section Map
116	- **§1 Intro**: Gap + contributions (causal map + differential nocuity + model×type interaction)
117	- **§2 Related Work**: Ambiguity taxonomies (NLP + RE) → Agent safety evaluation → Policy specification quality. Position vs DRIP-R
118	- **§3 Taxonomy**: 2-layer, 6-type taxonomy with cross-walk to Li et al. + Massey et al. + DRIP-R
119	- **§4 Method**: Matched-pair causal design, τ²-bench, 5 models (3 proprietary + 2 open-source), clause generation, perturbation control, cross-judge evaluation
120	- **§5 Results**: C1 (binary, +34.0pp, 5 models) → C2 (type hierarchy, 3-tier) → C3 (layer effect, modest but significant) → C4 (model×type interaction — star finding)
121	- **§6 Analysis**: C5 error analysis — qualitative failure modes per type. Ambiguity Blindness. Model-specific patterns.
122	- **§7 Discussion**: Differential nocuity theory. Safety training selectivity. Disambiguation channel framework. Limitations (2 domains, synthetic injection, LLM-as-judge).
123	- **§8 Conclusion**: All policy ambiguity is nocuous, but type AND model jointly determine risk level. Both type-aware auditing and model-specific risk assessment recommended.
124	
125	## Anticipated Reviewer Concerns
126	
127	### RC1: "Type effect could be artifact of taxonomy granularity"
128	**Response**: (a) Layer effect (Spec vs Ling ~19pp gap) is robust — holds even if individual types are reclassified. (b) 2-layer structure grounded in Li et al. + Massey et al. (c) Coreferential's low rate has structural explanation (disambiguation channels), not just noise. (d) TOST confirms types are NOT equivalent (0/15 pairs at ±10pp).
129	
130	### RC2: "Taxonomy is ad hoc / why these 6 types"
131	**Response**: 2-layer structure grounded in Li et al. 2024 (11-type NLP) + Massey et al. 2014 (6-type RE). Selection criteria: frequency in policy documents + theoretical distinctiveness. Explicit cross-walk to DRIP-R's 5 types. Operational definition handles ambiguity/vagueness boundary (Wasow 2005, Kennedy 2007).
132	
133	### RC3: "Only API models, no open-source"
134	**Response**: ✅ RESOLVED. 5-model coverage spans: frontier proprietary (gpt-5.4, claude-sonnet-4-6) + mid-tier proprietary (gpt-4.1) + open-source MoE (qwen3-235b) + open-source dense (deepseek-v3). Three providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Chinese open-source). Two architecture types (dense, MoE). Model×type interaction (C4) reveals rich cross-model patterns.
135	**Note [Reviewer 2026-05-20]**: Cross-judge asymmetry — Claude judged by gpt-5.4, gpt-5.4 judged by gpt-4.1. Must disclose in Method. plan_009 judge calibration measures this bias.
136	
137	### RC4: "Synthetic ambiguity injection lacks ecological validity"
138	**Response**: (a) Matched-pair design requires synthetic control for causal inference. (b) Reviewer-verified quality (Chantree-style). (c) CP clauses use both explicit labeling and naturalistic rule rewrites. (d) Full study mixes formats per Reviewer suggestion. (e) Realism validation: distribution comparison with DRIP-R natural ambiguities.
139	
140	### RC5: "τ²-bench limited to retail/airline"
141	**Response**: Acknowledged limitation. Two domains already show consistent effects. Cross-domain transfer is Future Work (Phase 3 classifier PoC, if time permits). DRIP-R also single-domain (retail).
142	
143	### RC6: "Binary effect is obvious — of course ambiguity causes errors"
144	**Response**: (a) No prior work quantifies effect SIZE for agent safety. +35-42pp is massive and non-trivial. (b) DRIP-R measures decision quality, not safety violations. (c) Prior work (PolicyBank, PhantomPolicy) studies different failure modes, not ambiguity-specific causation. (d) The interesting finding is C2: type DOES predict severity — specification-layer ambiguities are nearly twice as dangerous, connecting to disambiguation channel availability.
145	
146	### RC7: "Incompleteness matched-pair confound (information asymmetry)"
147	**Response**: (a) Dual-track analysis: primary analysis uses ambiguous-only cross-type comparison (avoids confound). (b) Incompleteness pairs constrained to minimal information addition. (c) Explicitly discussed as limitation for within-type effect size.
148	
149	### RC8: "RC attachment in coreferential overlaps with scopal / structural ambiguity"
150	**Response**: (a) Our scopal category is explicitly scoped to quantifier/negation/modal scope interactions, not syntactic attachment. (b) RC attachment in policies manifests as *referential* confusion (which entity does the clause modify?) not *scope* confusion (which operator takes wide scope?). (c) Li et al. 2024 distinguishes syntactic ambiguity (including RC attachment) from scopal ambiguity — our grouping follows their treatment that RC attachment is closer to coreferential than scopal in terms of downstream interpretation. (d) Empirically, if the distinction were problematic, coreferential and scopal would show identical violation patterns — the error analysis (C5) can test whether their failure modes differ.
151	
152	### RC9: "authorization_scope is just a subtype of incompleteness"
153	**Response**: (a) Incompleteness = missing conditions/exceptions/boundaries (structural absence). Authorization scope = ambiguous permission/role boundaries that ARE stated but vague (e.g., "authorized personnel" without specifying which functions). (b) The disambiguation pattern differs: incompleteness adds new conditions; auth_scope clarifies existing permission boundaries. (c) Empirically testable: if they were the same, their violation patterns and failure modes (C5) would be indistinguishable. (d) Report disambiguation length ratio per type as control variable in §4 Method.
154	
155	### RC10: "API sampling noise undermines reliability"
156	**Response**: ✅ RESOLVED. plan_006 ICC=0.919 [0.892, 0.940] (excellent). (a) Per-clause violation rates highly reproducible across 3 independent replicates. (b) Binary ICC=0.847 (good). (c) Both models show near-identical ICC (gpt-5.4: 0.921, gpt-4.1: 0.918). (d) Bootstrap CI + ICC double evidence. (e) Previously identified ±8pp noise is within expected variance given the ICC confidence intervals.
157	
158	### RC11: "Prompt sensitivity confound" [Dream A9 — best tier "strongest point"]
159	**Concern**: The +35-42pp effect is attributed entirely to ambiguity, but without a control condition using non-ambiguity perturbations (synonym substitution, clause reordering), the paper cannot cleanly distinguish ambiguity-specific harm from general prompt brittleness.
160	**Response**: ✅ RESOLVED. plan_010 perturbation control (120 episodes): Δ_perturb=3.33pp (CI contains 0) vs ambiguity Δ=36.5pp. Non-ambiguity surface changes cause zero meaningful effect. This is the strongest causal evidence in the agent safety literature.
161	
162	## Concept Naming (distill insight: 命名即贡献)
163	
164	Core phenomenon: **"Differential Nocuity"** — all policy ambiguity types are nocuous for LLM agents (+34.0pp, all 5 models), but vulnerability varies by BOTH type and model. Incompleteness is universally dangerous (46-62%), while auth_scope vulnerability depends dramatically on safety training (12% Claude to 64% GPT-5.4). Unlike human RE where organizational context renders most ambiguity innocuous, agents lack disambiguation channels AND their safety training creates type-specific blind spots.
165	
166	Secondary phenomenon: **"Ambiguity Blindness"** — agents process grammatically fluent ambiguous clauses without meta-cognitive awareness of the ambiguity, adopting surface interpretations. Contrasts with explicit rule conflicts where agents show awareness and choose conservatively.
167	
168	Tertiary phenomenon: **"Disambiguation Channel Framework"** [renamed from "Hypothesis" per Dream review SF-5] — the layer hierarchy reflects availability of external disambiguation: linguistic ambiguity (coreferential, lexical) can sometimes be resolved by tool responses, user context, or world knowledge; specification ambiguity (auth_scope, incompleteness) has no external resolution channel, forcing agents to guess. This is an explanatory framework supported by observational evidence (ICC pattern, failure mode distribution, coreferential boundary case), not a tested causal hypothesis. Future Work: manipulation experiment (inject spec-layer disambiguation info into tool responses, test if gap shrinks).
169	
170	Quaternary phenomenon: **"Systematic Nocuity"** [per Dream review SF-7] — B&K framework distinguishes nocuous (divergent interpretations) from innocuous (convergent). Our data reveals a third type: all models converge on the same WRONG interpretation (27% of ambiguous episodes). This is more dangerous than divergent nocuity — it's invisible in inter-model agreement metrics and appears "correct" until compared against ground truth. Proposed as B&K extension in Discussion.
171	
172	## Opening Hook Strategy (distill insight: 具体案例, 不要 "Recently...")
173	
174	Open with a concrete τ²-bench failure: e.g., a customer returns a customized item within the return window; the agent grants a full refund + free return shipping because the policy says "items may be returned within 30 days" (scopal: "items" scopes over all categories including custom). The unambiguous version specifies "standard items only" — agent correctly refuses. One word of ambiguity → $200 unauthorized refund.
175	
176	## Narrative Type: 突破局限型 (distill pattern, 5/8 papers)
177	
178	"DRIP-R classifies 5 ambiguity types and shows models disagree on interpretation → but does not measure whether this disagreement leads to safety violations. We close this gap — and find the answer is surprising: not all types are equal, specification-layer ambiguities are nearly twice as dangerous as linguistic-layer ones."
179	
180	## Benchmark Comparison Table (distill insight: 必有 feature matrix)
181	
182	| Feature | DRIP-R | PhantomPolicy | PolicyBank | AgentPex | **Ours** |
183	|---------|--------|---------------|------------|----------|----------|
184	| Ambiguity taxonomy | 5 RE types | — | 3 gap types | — | **6 types (2-layer)** |
185	| Causal design | — | — | — | — | **matched pairs** |
186	| Safety violation metric | — | binary | — | procedural | **3-tier severity** |
187	| Cross-type comparison | descriptive | — | — | — | **statistical (χ² + V)** |
188	| Models tested | 6 API | 4 API | 2 API | 2 API | **3 API + 2 open-source** |
189	| Domain | retail | mixed | retail | telecom/retail/airline | **retail + airline** |
190	
191	## Contribution Positioning (for EMNLP) [revised 2026-05-20 with 5-model data]
192	
193	1. **Causal quantification of ambiguity's safety impact**: First matched-pair causal study of policy ambiguity → agent safety violations. Binary effect +34.0pp (OR=15.1, p<0.0001) across 5 architecturally diverse models and 6 ambiguity types. Perturbation control (Δ_perturb=3.33pp) confirms ambiguity-specific causation. Strongest causal evidence in the agent safety literature.
194	2. **Differential Nocuity framework + Model × Type Interaction**: Not all ambiguity is equally dangerous, and not all models are equally vulnerable. 3-tier type hierarchy (incompleteness >> mid cluster >> coreferential). Model × type interaction reveals 52pp range in auth_scope vulnerability (Claude 12% → GPT-5.4 64%), while incompleteness remains universally dangerous (46-62%). Safety training differentially mitigates specific ambiguity types. Connects Berry & Kamsties nocuous ambiguity theory to modern safety alignment.
195	3. **Type-specific failure mode taxonomy + Ambiguity Blindness**: 245 traces across 2 models and 2 domains reveal type-diagnostic failure signatures: spec-layer → guess-and-act (unauthorized_escalation, assumption_based_action); ling-layer → misparse-and-apply (scope_misapplication). Agents show <5-11% awareness of ambiguity ("Ambiguity Blindness"), with >88% surface adoption and <1% user escalation. Practical implication: ambiguity detection must be externalized.
196	
197	NOTE: C3 (layer effect, Δ=6.08pp) is a component finding supporting contribution #2. The MODEL × TYPE interaction (C4) is now MORE central than the layer main effect. "Disambiguation channel" is an explanatory framework (not hypothesis — per SF-5). DeBERTa classifier, if included, is a preliminary PoC appendix, not a contribution.

# Paper Framing — policy_ambiguity_safety

> 最后更新: 2026-05-20 19:30 UTC | 状态: 5-model analysis complete, C3/C4 framing revised
> 目标: EMNLP 2026 (ARR Aug cycle, DDL ~Aug 3)
> Dream: dream_20260520T112859 — best 3.5 / median 3.0 / worst 2.5 (pre-pivot; re-dream needed)
> 5-model: 2,997 episodes, C1 confirmed (+34.0pp, 5 models), C4 upgraded (model×type interaction)

## Core Insight

Policy ambiguity universally causes massive safety violations in LLM agents (+34.0pp across 5 architecturally diverse models), with a significant type hierarchy (incompleteness 53.6% >> coreferential 31.6%). Specification-layer types are more dangerous on average (Δ=6.08pp, p=0.017), but the deeper finding is a **model × type interaction**: authorization scope vulnerability varies 52pp across models (12% Claude to 64% GPT-5.4), revealing that safety training differentially mitigates specific ambiguity types, while incompleteness remains universally dangerous. This interaction connects Berry & Kamsties' nocuous ambiguity theory to modern safety alignment and suggests both type-aware triage AND model-aware risk assessment.

## Title (Working)

"Not All Policy Ambiguity Is Equal: Differential Vulnerability Profiles Across LLM Agent Families"

Alternative: "Differential Nocuity: How Ambiguity Type and Model Architecture Shape Safety Violations in LLM Agents"

Note: Pivoted from "Uniformly Nocuous" → "Specification-Layer Dominant" (2-model) → "Differential Nocuity with Model Interaction" (5-model). The model × type interaction is the novel finding that elevates the paper beyond simple effect demonstration.

## Core Claims

### C1: Binary Effect (PRIMARY — confirmed, 5 models)
Ambiguous policy specifications cause massive safety violation rate increases compared to unambiguous matched variants. Effect: +34.0pp (5-model), McNemar OR=15.1 (CI: [10.78, 21.17]), p<0.0001. Holds across all 6 types and all 5 models.
- **Evidence**: 2,997 episodes across 5 models × 6 types × 2 conditions. Bootstrap CI: [+31.2pp, +36.9pp].
- **Per-model**: Claude +25.7pp, Qwen3 +32.4pp, GPT-4.1 +34.7pp, GPT-5.4 +38.3pp, DeepSeek +39.0pp — all p<10^-17.
- **Strength**: Extremely strong. Replicated across 5 architecturally diverse models (proprietary dense, open-source MoE, open-source dense), 6 types, 2 domains. No exceptions.
- **Causal backing**: Matched-pair design + perturbation control (plan_010, Δ_perturb=3.33pp, PASS) → strongest causal inference in the literature.
- **Logistic regression**: condition_amb coef=2.278, z=19.65, p<0.001 — ambiguity is the dominant predictor even after controlling for token delta, model, and type.

### C2: Type Hierarchy (SECONDARY — confirmed, 5 models)
**PIVOTED from uniformity null.** 6-type hierarchy significant: omnibus χ²=28.02, p=3.6×10^-5, V=0.137 (small but well-powered: actual power=0.993, MDE=0.093). 3-tier structure emerges from TOST analysis.
- **Evidence**: 2,997 episodes (5 models × 6 types × 2 conditions, ambiguous only: 1,499 episodes)
  - **High tier**: incompleteness 53.6% (standout — universally dangerous across all models)
  - **Mid tier**: lexical 42.8%, auth_scope 41.6%, scopal 39.4%, CP 36.8% — pairwise equivalent at ±15pp
  - **Low tier**: coreferential 31.6% (lowest — partial disambiguation via tool responses)
- **TOST structure**: ±15pp: 8/15 equivalent, 7/15 non-equivalent. ±10pp: 4/15 equivalent, 11/15 non-equivalent. Types are NOT interchangeable.
- **V=0.137 context**: Below 0.20 threshold but well-powered (power=0.993). The type effect is real but small — the 3-tier structure captures it better than a single V statistic. The heterogeneity is driven by the extremes (incompleteness 53.6% vs coreferential 31.6% = 22pp gap).
- **Coreferential as boundary case**: 31.6% violation rate is the lowest but still substantial (+18.7pp vs unambiguous). Agents partially disambiguate via tool responses and cautious strategies. Conservative_refusal rate 6-11% (vs avg 2-3%).
- **Model-dependence of type rankings**: Type rankings are NOT identical across models. Incompleteness is top-2 for ALL models, but auth_scope ranges from #1 (GPT-5.4, DeepSeek) to #6 (Claude). See C4.

### C3: Layer Effect (TERTIARY — suggestive, fragile under within-judge analysis)
**[2026-05-20 REVISED with 5-model data + within-judge check]** Specification-layer ambiguities cause more violations than linguistic-layer on average, but the effect is modest, model-dependent, and fragile under subgroup analysis.
- **Evidence (5-model aggregate)**: Spec 44.0% vs Ling 37.9%, Δ=6.08pp, CI [1.14, 11.02], χ²=5.73, p=0.017, V=0.062 (small), OR=1.29 [1.05, 1.58].
- **Within-judge fragility**: gpt-4.1 judged group (gpt-5.4+DeepSeek): Δ=+8.0pp, p=0.059 (marginal). gpt-5.4 judged group (gpt-4.1+Claude+Qwen3): Δ=+4.8pp, p=0.157 (n.s.). Pooled significance may partly reflect between-judge variance or insufficient within-group power. Paper表述: "suggestive" or "a moderate tendency," NOT "confirmed." Disclose within-judge non-significance in Limitations.
- **Per-model layer gaps** (THE KEY FINDING — feeds C4):
  - GPT-5.4: +14.0pp (spec 48.0% vs ling 34.0%) — strong
  - GPT-4.1: +12.0pp (spec 46.7% vs ling 34.7%) — strong
  - Claude: +3.3pp (spec 32.0% vs ling 28.7%) — weak
  - DeepSeek: +2.0pp (spec 50.7% vs ling 48.7%) — negligible
  - Qwen3: -0.9pp (spec 42.7% vs ling 43.6%) — reversed!
- **Root cause**: auth_scope is the primary driver. GPT models have extremely high auth_scope rates (46-64%), inflating their spec-layer average. Claude (12%) and Qwen3 (26%) have low auth_scope, so their spec-layer advantage disappears.
- **Framing decision**: C3 is NOT "spec-layer nearly twice as dangerous" (that was 2-model artifact). The correct framing is: "Specification-layer types are significantly more dangerous on average (Δ=6.08pp, p=0.017), but this aggregate masks a model × type interaction where the gap varies from +14pp (GPT-5.4) to -1pp (Qwen3). The interaction, not the main effect, is the theoretically interesting finding (see C4)."
- **Info delta as mediator** [MF-2]: Token delta significant in 5-model logistic regression (coef=0.022, z=3.49, p=0.0005). Spec-layer clauses require more tokens to disambiguate (auth_scope 36.1, incomp 34.6 vs coref 7.8 tokens). Info delta partially mediates but doesn't eliminate the condition effect (condition_amb coef=2.278 dominates).
- **Layer overlap persists**: CP (36.8%, spec) < scopal (39.4%, ling). Mid-tier cluster spans both layers. Layer effect is driven by extremes: incompleteness (53.6%, spec) vs coreferential (31.6%, ling).
- **ICC convergent evidence** [plan_006]: Per-type ICC mirrors layer hierarchy — Ling-layer ICC all excellent (scopal 0.989, lexical 0.981, coref 0.976), Spec-layer ICC all good (auth 0.857, CP 0.856, incomp 0.807). Spec-layer less reproducible — agents guess differently each run when external disambiguation channels are absent.
- **CL connection**: Parallels pragmatics vs semantics distinction. Good-enough processing (Ferreira et al. 2002). Disambiguation channel framework: linguistic ambiguity has partial external resolution; specification ambiguity forces guessing.

### C4: Model × Type Interaction (UPGRADED — star finding, 5 models complete)
**[2026-05-20 DEFINITIVE, 5/5 models]** Models show significantly different vulnerability profiles despite universal binary effect. The interaction is the paper's most novel finding.
- **Model main effect**: Overall χ²=31.02, p=3.0×10^-6, V=0.102. Ambiguous-only: χ²=24.01, p=7.9×10^-5.
  - Vulnerability ranking: Claude 30.3% < GPT-5.4 41.0% ≈ GPT-4.1 40.7% < Qwen3 43.1% < DeepSeek 49.7%
  - Bootstrap CI confirms: Claude significantly lower than all others; DeepSeek significantly higher than GPT models.
- **Model × Type interaction matrix** (ambiguous condition, violation rates):
  ```
  Type                  GPT-5.4  GPT-4.1  Claude  Qwen3   DeepSeek
  authorization_scope     64%     46%      12%     26%     60%
  conditional_precedence  34%     36%      36%     40%     38%
  incompleteness          46%     58%      48%     62%     54%
  lexical                 42%     34%      32%     52%     54%
  coreferential           18%     32%      22%     42%     44%
  scopal                  42%     38%      32%     37%     48%
  ```
- **Key interaction patterns**:
  - **auth_scope**: 52pp range (Claude 12% → GPT-5.4 64%). The MODEL-DIFFERENTIATING type. Claude's RLHF appears to specifically train authorization boundary awareness.
  - **coreferential**: 26pp range (GPT-5.4 18% → DeepSeek 44%). Second most model-dependent. Open-source models struggle more with referential ambiguity.
  - **incompleteness**: Universally high (46-62%, 16pp range). ALL models fail on missing information — safety training doesn't help when information literally isn't there.
  - **CP**: Most model-invariant (34-40%, 6pp range). Explicit rule conflicts treated similarly by all architectures.
- **Per-model type χ²** (which models show type-specific vulnerability patterns):
  - GPT-5.4: χ²=23.44, p=0.0003, V=0.28 — strongest type differentiation (very high auth_scope, very low coref)
  - Claude: χ²=17.87, p=0.003, V=0.24 — strong differentiation (very low auth_scope, moderate others)
  - Qwen3: χ²=15.89, p=0.007, V=0.23 — moderate differentiation (high incomp+lex, low auth_scope)
  - GPT-4.1: χ²=9.89, p=0.078, V=0.18 — borderline
  - DeepSeek: χ²=6.31, p=0.277, V=0.14 — NOT significant (uniformly high across all types)
- **Fleiss κ = 0.384 (fair agreement)**: Models only moderately agree on which specific clauses trigger violations. The binary effect is universal, but the WHICH-clauses question is model-dependent.
- **Theoretical implications**: (1) Safety training differentially addresses specific ambiguity types — Claude's auth_scope robustness suggests authorization boundary handling was explicitly or implicitly trained. (2) Incompleteness is a "safety training blind spot" — all models fail equally. (3) DeepSeek's uniform vulnerability suggests less type-specific safety training.
- **Framing**: C4 from "models agree" → "Models show systematically different vulnerability profiles. The binary effect is universal, but HOW models fail depends on the intersection of ambiguity type and safety training approach. auth_scope is the canary type — most sensitive to safety training quality."
- **Evidence from plan_005**: 2-model failure modes consistent (5/6 dominant modes identical). 5-model failure mode analysis pending.
- **Layer effect moderation**: C3's aggregate layer gap (6.08pp) is driven by GPT models' high auth_scope rates. The layer effect is itself model-dependent (GPT +12-14pp, Claude +3pp, Qwen3 reversed), making the MODEL × TYPE interaction more fundamental than the LAYER main effect.

### C5: Error Analysis (CONFIRMED — EMNLP core)
Different ambiguity types produce qualitatively different failure modes with type-specific signatures. plan_005 (123+122 violation traces across gpt-5.4 and gpt-4.1, confidence=0.94).
- **Evidence**: plan_005 complete (gpt-5.4: 123 traces, gpt-4.1: 122 traces). Key findings:
  - **Type-specific failure signatures**: auth_scope → unauthorized_escalation (72%/83%); incompleteness → assumption_based_action (61%/66%); scopal → scope_misapplication (76%/74%); lexical → assumption_based_action (71%/53%); CP → scope_misapplication (41%/28%) + arbitrary_rule_selection (29%/28%); coreferential → scope_misapplication (44%) / assumption_based_action (38%)
  - **Cross-model consistency**: 5/6 types share the same dominant failure mode across gpt-5.4 and gpt-4.1. Only coreferential diverges (scope_misapplication vs assumption_based_action). Overall mode distribution nearly identical: both ~33% assumption_based_action, ~26-32% unauthorized_escalation, ~25-28% scope_misapplication. Failure mode profiles are type-specific, not model-specific.
  - **Layer mechanism**: Ling-layer dominated by scope_misapplication (39% ling avg vs 15% spec avg) = "misparse"; Spec-layer dominated by unauthorized_escalation + assumption_based_action = "active guessing" → explains higher violation rates
  - **Ambiguity Blindness empirically confirmed**: awareness rate gpt-5.4=4.1%, gpt-4.1=10.7% (both very low); surface_adoption >88% all types both models; escalate_to_user <1%. Nuance: gpt-4.1 (mid-tier) shows 2.6× higher awareness than gpt-5.4 (frontier) — awareness may inversely correlate with action-orientation (frontier models more "confident," act without hesitation)
  - **Cross-domain consistency**: airline vs retail failure mode profiles Δ < 13pp (unauthorized_escalation shows largest domain effect: retail 38.6% vs airline 26.1%)
  - **Coreferential boundary**: conservative_refusal 6-11% (vs avg 2-3%) partially explains low violation rate — agents sometimes pause rather than guess. N=25 combined traces show no single dominant failure mode (flat distribution: scope_misapplication 32%, assumption_based_action 28%, unauthorized_escalation 16%) — contrasts with other types' sharp signatures, reflecting the diversity of resolution strategies for referential ambiguity
  - **Lexical surprise**: 53-71% assumption_based_action — agents treat word ambiguity as information gap, not misparse
- **Automated inter-coder agreement** [MF-5, Reviewer-validated]: Cross-coding 60 traces (gpt-5.4 vs gpt-4.1 as independent coders). 4-category merged: 80% agreement, Cohen's κ=0.594 (moderate). κ deflated by kappa paradox — lexical 91.7% agreement → κ=0.0 (11/12 same label, chance agreement also high), scopal 100% agreement → κ undefined. True disagreement concentrated at unauthorized_escalation ↔ inappropriate_action boundary in auth_scope (κ=0.054) and incompleteness (κ=0.233).
  - **Reporting strategy** [Reviewer recommendation]: (1) Compute Gwet's AC1 as primary metric (designed for kappa paradox, expected 0.70-0.75); (2) Report 80% agreement + 5/6 dominant mode consistency as headline validity evidence; (3) Report κ honestly with kappa paradox caveat; (4) Auth_scope failure mode: soften to "dominated by boundary-exceeding behaviors (unauthorized_escalation or inappropriate_action, >90%)" instead of specific percentages; (5) Fine-grained 6-type as appendix with "automated coding" caveat.
  - **C5 safety**: Ambiguity Blindness (<5-11%), surface_adoption (>88%), layer mechanism (ling→scope vs spec→escalation) all robust. Fine-grained per-type percentages unreliable at κ=0.594. Plan_009 human anchor (20-30 failure mode traces) would upgrade from "moderate automated" to validated.
- **EMNLP value**: Highest. Provides the linguistic WHY behind the quantitative WHAT. Cross-model + cross-domain consistency elevates from anecdotal to systematic finding. "Ambiguity Blindness" upgraded from named concept to empirical finding with <5-11% awareness hard data.

## Narrative Structure (CL-first for EMNLP)

### Intro Logic Chain
1. Agent policies are written in NL → contain ambiguity (established)
2. Prior work classifies ambiguity types in policies (DRIP-R, Li et al., Massey et al.) but doesn't measure safety impact
3. Berry & Kamsties (2003): ambiguity is nocuous (divergent interpretations) or innocuous (convergent). In human RE, shared organizational context makes most ambiguity innocuous.
4. **Gap**: LLM agents lack shared context. Are policy ambiguities nocuous for agents? Does type matter? Does it depend on the model?
5. **This paper**: First causal, type-granularity, cross-model study. Matched-pair design + perturbation control isolates ambiguity effect. 5 models × 6 types.
6. **Core findings**: (a) All ambiguity is nocuous (+34.0pp, 5 models), (b) type DOES predict severity — 3-tier hierarchy with incompleteness most dangerous, (c) models show dramatically different vulnerability profiles — auth_scope varies 52pp across models, suggesting safety training differentially addresses ambiguity types, (d) while incompleteness remains universally dangerous, a "safety training blind spot."

### Section Map
- **§1 Intro**: Gap + contributions (causal map + differential nocuity + model×type interaction)
- **§2 Related Work**: Ambiguity taxonomies (NLP + RE) → Agent safety evaluation → Policy specification quality. Position vs DRIP-R
- **§3 Taxonomy**: 2-layer, 6-type taxonomy with cross-walk to Li et al. + Massey et al. + DRIP-R
- **§4 Method**: Matched-pair causal design, τ²-bench, 5 models (3 proprietary + 2 open-source), clause generation, perturbation control, cross-judge evaluation
- **§5 Results**: C1 (binary, +34.0pp, 5 models) → C2 (type hierarchy, 3-tier) → C3 (layer effect, modest but significant) → C4 (model×type interaction — star finding)
- **§6 Analysis**: C5 error analysis — qualitative failure modes per type. Ambiguity Blindness. Model-specific patterns.
- **§7 Discussion**: Differential nocuity theory. Safety training selectivity. Disambiguation channel framework. Limitations (2 domains, synthetic injection, LLM-as-judge).
- **§8 Conclusion**: All policy ambiguity is nocuous, but type AND model jointly determine risk level. Both type-aware auditing and model-specific risk assessment recommended.

## Anticipated Reviewer Concerns

### RC1: "Type effect could be artifact of taxonomy granularity"
**Response**: (a) Layer effect (Spec vs Ling ~19pp gap) is robust — holds even if individual types are reclassified. (b) 2-layer structure grounded in Li et al. + Massey et al. (c) Coreferential's low rate has structural explanation (disambiguation channels), not just noise. (d) TOST confirms types are NOT equivalent (0/15 pairs at ±10pp).

### RC2: "Taxonomy is ad hoc / why these 6 types"
**Response**: 2-layer structure grounded in Li et al. 2024 (11-type NLP) + Massey et al. 2014 (6-type RE). Selection criteria: frequency in policy documents + theoretical distinctiveness. Explicit cross-walk to DRIP-R's 5 types. Operational definition handles ambiguity/vagueness boundary (Wasow 2005, Kennedy 2007).

### RC3: "Only API models, no open-source"
**Response**: ✅ RESOLVED. 5-model coverage spans: frontier proprietary (gpt-5.4, claude-sonnet-4-6) + mid-tier proprietary (gpt-4.1) + open-source MoE (qwen3-235b) + open-source dense (deepseek-v3). Three providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Chinese open-source). Two architecture types (dense, MoE). Model×type interaction (C4) reveals rich cross-model patterns.
**Note [Reviewer 2026-05-20]**: Cross-judge asymmetry — Claude judged by gpt-5.4, gpt-5.4 judged by gpt-4.1. Must disclose in Method. plan_009 judge calibration measures this bias.

### RC4: "Synthetic ambiguity injection lacks ecological validity"
**Response**: (a) Matched-pair design requires synthetic control for causal inference. (b) Reviewer-verified quality (Chantree-style). (c) CP clauses use both explicit labeling and naturalistic rule rewrites. (d) Full study mixes formats per Reviewer suggestion. (e) Realism validation: distribution comparison with DRIP-R natural ambiguities.

### RC5: "τ²-bench limited to retail/airline"
**Response**: Acknowledged limitation. Two domains already show consistent effects. Cross-domain transfer is Future Work (Phase 3 classifier PoC, if time permits). DRIP-R also single-domain (retail).

### RC6: "Binary effect is obvious — of course ambiguity causes errors"
**Response**: (a) No prior work quantifies effect SIZE for agent safety. +35-42pp is massive and non-trivial. (b) DRIP-R measures decision quality, not safety violations. (c) Prior work (PolicyBank, PhantomPolicy) studies different failure modes, not ambiguity-specific causation. (d) The interesting finding is C2: type DOES predict severity — specification-layer ambiguities are nearly twice as dangerous, connecting to disambiguation channel availability.

### RC7: "Incompleteness matched-pair confound (information asymmetry)"
**Response**: (a) Dual-track analysis: primary analysis uses ambiguous-only cross-type comparison (avoids confound). (b) Incompleteness pairs constrained to minimal information addition. (c) Explicitly discussed as limitation for within-type effect size.

### RC8: "RC attachment in coreferential overlaps with scopal / structural ambiguity"
**Response**: (a) Our scopal category is explicitly scoped to quantifier/negation/modal scope interactions, not syntactic attachment. (b) RC attachment in policies manifests as *referential* confusion (which entity does the clause modify?) not *scope* confusion (which operator takes wide scope?). (c) Li et al. 2024 distinguishes syntactic ambiguity (including RC attachment) from scopal ambiguity — our grouping follows their treatment that RC attachment is closer to coreferential than scopal in terms of downstream interpretation. (d) Empirically, if the distinction were problematic, coreferential and scopal would show identical violation patterns — the error analysis (C5) can test whether their failure modes differ.

### RC9: "authorization_scope is just a subtype of incompleteness"
**Response**: (a) Incompleteness = missing conditions/exceptions/boundaries (structural absence). Authorization scope = ambiguous permission/role boundaries that ARE stated but vague (e.g., "authorized personnel" without specifying which functions). (b) The disambiguation pattern differs: incompleteness adds new conditions; auth_scope clarifies existing permission boundaries. (c) Empirically testable: if they were the same, their violation patterns and failure modes (C5) would be indistinguishable. (d) Report disambiguation length ratio per type as control variable in §4 Method.

### RC10: "API sampling noise undermines reliability"
**Response**: ✅ RESOLVED. plan_006 ICC=0.919 [0.892, 0.940] (excellent). (a) Per-clause violation rates highly reproducible across 3 independent replicates. (b) Binary ICC=0.847 (good). (c) Both models show near-identical ICC (gpt-5.4: 0.921, gpt-4.1: 0.918). (d) Bootstrap CI + ICC double evidence. (e) Previously identified ±8pp noise is within expected variance given the ICC confidence intervals.

### RC11: "Prompt sensitivity confound" [Dream A9 — best tier "strongest point"]
**Concern**: The +35-42pp effect is attributed entirely to ambiguity, but without a control condition using non-ambiguity perturbations (synonym substitution, clause reordering), the paper cannot cleanly distinguish ambiguity-specific harm from general prompt brittleness.
**Response**: ✅ RESOLVED. plan_010 perturbation control (120 episodes): Δ_perturb=3.33pp (CI contains 0) vs ambiguity Δ=36.5pp. Non-ambiguity surface changes cause zero meaningful effect. This is the strongest causal evidence in the agent safety literature.

## Concept Naming (distill insight: 命名即贡献)

Core phenomenon: **"Differential Nocuity"** — all policy ambiguity types are nocuous for LLM agents (+34.0pp, all 5 models), but vulnerability varies by BOTH type and model. Incompleteness is universally dangerous (46-62%), while auth_scope vulnerability depends dramatically on safety training (12% Claude to 64% GPT-5.4). Unlike human RE where organizational context renders most ambiguity innocuous, agents lack disambiguation channels AND their safety training creates type-specific blind spots.

Secondary phenomenon: **"Ambiguity Blindness"** — agents process grammatically fluent ambiguous clauses without meta-cognitive awareness of the ambiguity, adopting surface interpretations. Contrasts with explicit rule conflicts where agents show awareness and choose conservatively.

Tertiary phenomenon: **"Disambiguation Channel Framework"** [renamed from "Hypothesis" per Dream review SF-5] — the layer hierarchy reflects availability of external disambiguation: linguistic ambiguity (coreferential, lexical) can sometimes be resolved by tool responses, user context, or world knowledge; specification ambiguity (auth_scope, incompleteness) has no external resolution channel, forcing agents to guess. This is an explanatory framework supported by observational evidence (ICC pattern, failure mode distribution, coreferential boundary case), not a tested causal hypothesis. Future Work: manipulation experiment (inject spec-layer disambiguation info into tool responses, test if gap shrinks).

Quaternary phenomenon: **"Systematic Nocuity"** [per Dream review SF-7] — B&K framework distinguishes nocuous (divergent interpretations) from innocuous (convergent). Our data reveals a third type: all models converge on the same WRONG interpretation (27% of ambiguous episodes). This is more dangerous than divergent nocuity — it's invisible in inter-model agreement metrics and appears "correct" until compared against ground truth. Proposed as B&K extension in Discussion.

## Opening Hook Strategy (distill insight: 具体案例, 不要 "Recently...")

Open with a concrete τ²-bench failure: e.g., a customer returns a customized item within the return window; the agent grants a full refund + free return shipping because the policy says "items may be returned within 30 days" (scopal: "items" scopes over all categories including custom). The unambiguous version specifies "standard items only" — agent correctly refuses. One word of ambiguity → $200 unauthorized refund.

## Narrative Type: 突破局限型 (distill pattern, 5/8 papers)

"DRIP-R classifies 5 ambiguity types and shows models disagree on interpretation → but does not measure whether this disagreement leads to safety violations. We close this gap — and find the answer is surprising: not all types are equal, specification-layer ambiguities are nearly twice as dangerous as linguistic-layer ones."

## Benchmark Comparison Table (distill insight: 必有 feature matrix)

| Feature | DRIP-R | PhantomPolicy | PolicyBank | AgentPex | **Ours** |
|---------|--------|---------------|------------|----------|----------|
| Ambiguity taxonomy | 5 RE types | — | 3 gap types | — | **6 types (2-layer)** |
| Causal design | — | — | — | — | **matched pairs** |
| Safety violation metric | — | binary | — | procedural | **3-tier severity** |
| Cross-type comparison | descriptive | — | — | — | **statistical (χ² + V)** |
| Models tested | 6 API | 4 API | 2 API | 2 API | **3 API + 2 open-source** |
| Domain | retail | mixed | retail | telecom/retail/airline | **retail + airline** |

## Contribution Positioning (for EMNLP) [revised 2026-05-20 with 5-model data]

1. **Causal quantification of ambiguity's safety impact**: First matched-pair causal study of policy ambiguity → agent safety violations. Binary effect +34.0pp (OR=15.1, p<0.0001) across 5 architecturally diverse models and 6 ambiguity types. Perturbation control (Δ_perturb=3.33pp) confirms ambiguity-specific causation. Strongest causal evidence in the agent safety literature.
2. **Differential Nocuity framework + Model × Type Interaction**: Not all ambiguity is equally dangerous, and not all models are equally vulnerable. 3-tier type hierarchy (incompleteness >> mid cluster >> coreferential). Model × type interaction reveals 52pp range in auth_scope vulnerability (Claude 12% → GPT-5.4 64%), while incompleteness remains universally dangerous (46-62%). Safety training differentially mitigates specific ambiguity types. Connects Berry & Kamsties nocuous ambiguity theory to modern safety alignment.
3. **Type-specific failure mode taxonomy + Ambiguity Blindness**: 245 traces across 2 models and 2 domains reveal type-diagnostic failure signatures: spec-layer → guess-and-act (unauthorized_escalation, assumption_based_action); ling-layer → misparse-and-apply (scope_misapplication). Agents show <5-11% awareness of ambiguity ("Ambiguity Blindness"), with >88% surface adoption and <1% user escalation. Practical implication: ambiguity detection must be externalized.

NOTE: C3 (layer effect, Δ=6.08pp) is a component finding supporting contribution #2. The MODEL × TYPE interaction (C4) is now MORE central than the layer main effect. "Disambiguation channel" is an explanatory framework (not hypothesis — per SF-5). DeBERTa classifier, if included, is a preliminary PoC appendix, not a contribution.

## Required Reference Expansion [Dream A2 + MF-4 RE literature gap]

Current plan has thin references. Must add (≥25 total in final paper):
- **Nocuous ambiguity detection (CRITICAL — MF-4)**: Chantree, Nuseibeh, de Roeck & Willis (2006, ASE) — first computational nocuous ambiguity detection; Chantree et al. (2008, RLAC) — expanded. Direct lineage to our DeBERTa classifier.
- **Cross-domain RE ambiguity**: Ferrari, Spagnolo & Gnesi (2017-2019, ASE) — NLP-based cross-domain ambiguity detection. NLP4RE community work.
- **Good-enough processing**: Ferreira, Bailey & Ferraro (2002); Ferreira & Patson (2007)
- **LLM garden-path (SF-6)**: Li et al. (2024) — incremental comprehension of garden-path sentences by LLMs. Directly relevant to how LLMs process ambiguity.
- **Anaphoric ambiguity (SF-6)**: Poesio & Artstein (2005, 2008) — annotation of anaphoric ambiguity. Poesio (2004) "Ambiguity" encyclopedia entry.
- **Surprisal/expectation-based**: Levy (2008); Hale (2001)
- **Instruction-following robustness**: Zhou et al. (IFEval, 2023); Qin et al. (ToolBench, 2024)
- **Prompt sensitivity**: Sclar et al. (2024); Lu et al. (2022)
- **Broader agent safety**: R-Judge, ToolEmu, InjecAgent
- **Formal semantics of vagueness**: Lassiter & Goodman (2017)
- **Garden-path**: Frazier & Rayner (1982)
- **Ambiguity detection**: Willis et al. (2008); Ezzini et al. (TAPHSIR, 2022)
- **Year verification needed**: Massey et al. — §1 引用 2013 vs 后文 2014, 需确认正确年份

## Code/Data Release Plan [Dream A6 — three-tier consistent]

Must commit to releasing:
1. All 300 clause pairs (ambiguous + unambiguous variants) with type labels
2. Evaluation scripts (τ²-bench integration, cross-judge pipeline)
3. Statistical analysis code (all tests, bootstrap CI computation)
4. Agent trace samples (anonymized) for reproducibility of C5

## Figure Plan [Dream A12]

Minimum figures for paper (zero-figure paper flagged in dream):
1. **Figure 1**: System architecture / experimental pipeline overview (§4 Method)
2. **Figure 2**: Forest plot — per-type binary effect sizes with 95% CI (§5 C1)
3. **Figure 3**: Model × Type heatmap — violation rates across 4 models × 6 types (§5 C4)
4. **Figure 4**: Visibility mechanism — CP vs scopal violation rates + trace evidence (§5 C3)
5. **Figure 5**: Failure mode × type stacked bar/Sankey — per-type failure mode distribution (§6 C5)
6. **Figure 6**: Cross-model failure mode consistency — side-by-side gpt-5.4 vs gpt-4.1 per-type distributions showing 5/6 convergence (§6 C5, supports C4)
7. **Figure 7**: Annotated trace pair — CP (conflict detection) vs scopal (surface adoption) (§6 C5)

## Berry & Kamsties Operationalization Note [Dream best Q5]

Berry & Kamsties define nocuity as inter-reader divergence. Our design measures agent-vs-intent deviation. Full study should additionally test whether different models adopt different readings of the same ambiguous clause (true inter-model nocuity). If 4 models produce 4 different interpretations of the same clause → true nocuity. If all 4 adopt the same wrong interpretation → systematic bias, still nocuous but for different reason. Report inter-model agreement on ambiguous clauses as supplementary analysis.

## Contingency Framing [RESOLVED — Scenario C occurred]

> plan_002 结果: Scenario C 发生（omnibus p=0.0001, 所有类型 nocuous 但 severity 有显著差异）。
> Framing 已 pivot 到 "Differential Nocuity" + "Layer Hierarchy" (D020)。本节仅保留历史记录。

## Claude Baseline — RESOLVED [2026-05-20]

✅ Claude works via OpenRouter proxy (47.94.22.126/v1) with provider prefix `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6`. 600 episodes complete (plan_002c). Claude shows lowest overall vulnerability (30.3%) and remarkable auth_scope robustness (12% vs GPT-5.4 64%).

17	---
18	
19	# 论文写作风格规范
20	
21	> 核心哲学：**论文是一个有说服力的故事，不是实验报告。** 审稿人在几十秒内判断论文价值——如果 Abstract 和 Introduction 读起来像实验日志，论文就已经失败了。
22	
23	---
24	
25	## 一、总体写作哲学
26	
27	### 1.1 故事驱动，不是数据堆砌
28	
29	- 论文必须以"故事线"为核心展开：问题 → 洞察 → 方法 → 验证
30	- 禁止大量实验数据堆砌——每个数字出现必须服务于叙事推进
31	- 附录内容必须在正文中有明确引用且融入叙事，禁止简单堆砌
32	- 如果附录数据对核心叙事有重大影响，根据附录数据调整论文 framing
33	
34	### 1.2 主线统一性
35	
36	- 当 idea 在研究过程中发生变化后，**必须重审全文逻辑**
37	- 常见问题：Introduction 讲的故事 A，Method 做的是故事 B，Results 又在讲故事 C
38	- 修复方式：从最终实验结论反推，重写 Introduction 的问题定义和动机
39	- 每次 idea 调整后检查：Abstract → Introduction → Method → Results → Discussion → Conclusion 是否形成一条连贯主线
40	
41	### 1.3 专有名词必须有定义
42	
43	- 首次出现的专有名词/缩写必须给出完整定义和解释
44	- Abstract 中使用的缩写也必须在 Abstract 内定义（如 LLM = Large Language Model）
45	- 不能假设读者知道你自己定义的术语——论文从来没解释过的概念不能直接使用
46	- 通用规则：如果一个非标准术语第一次出现时没有括号定义，就是写作 bug
47	
48	### 1.4 写作前必读同类优秀论文
49	
50	- 每个章节动笔前，找 **2-3 篇目标会议近 1-2 年的高分论文**作为风格参考——同类问题或同类方法皆可
51	- 重点学：
52	  - Abstract 怎么用最少篇幅讲完故事
53	  - Introduction 怎么从大问题切入到具体贡献
54	  - Related Work 怎么 positioning 自己（不是 survey）
55	  - Table/Figure 怎么压缩信息密度
56	- **不是抄袭**，是学习同行的故事节奏和审美——不同子领域叙事节奏差异很大
57	- 实操：Paper Agent 可以从 `literature_map.yaml` 中挑 `role=foundation` 或 `role=direct-competitor` 的论文，把 `{title, venue, year, abstract}` 附在 Worker 的 task_prompt 中作为概念参考；如需学习写作风格本身，让 Worker 通过 WebSearch 取得论文链接并 fetch 全文
58	
59	---
60	
61	## 二、Abstract 写作规范
62	
63	### 2.1 四个必答问题（150-250 words）
64	
65	Abstract 必须在很短的篇幅内清楚回答：
66	1. **研究什么问题** — 1-2 句话交代背景和痛点
67	2. **为什么重要** — 现有方法的不足（不用写太多）
68	3. **本文提出什么** — 核心贡献的关键机制（简要，不堆砌细节）
69	4. **结果说明什么** — 用具体实验结论支撑贡献
70	
71	### 2.2 禁忌
72	
73	- **禁止堆砌数据**：Abstract 不是 Results 的缩写。最多引用 2-3 个关键数字，要服务于 claim
74	- **禁止过度宣传**：不说 "revolutionary"、"groundbreaking"
75	- **禁止写成 Introduction 的缩写**：Abstract 是独立阅读单元
76	- **禁止术语堆积**：如果审稿人几十秒内判断不出价值，就失败了

# 论文写作风格规范

> 核心哲学：**论文是一个有说服力的故事，不是实验报告。** 审稿人在几十秒内判断论文价值——如果 Abstract 和 Introduction 读起来像实验日志，论文就已经失败了。

---

## 一、总体写作哲学

### 1.1 故事驱动，不是数据堆砌

- 论文必须以"故事线"为核心展开：问题 → 洞察 → 方法 → 验证
- 禁止大量实验数据堆砌——每个数字出现必须服务于叙事推进
- 附录内容必须在正文中有明确引用且融入叙事，禁止简单堆砌
- 如果附录数据对核心叙事有重大影响，根据附录数据调整论文 framing

### 1.2 主线统一性

- 当 idea 在研究过程中发生变化后，**必须重审全文逻辑**
- 常见问题：Introduction 讲的故事 A，Method 做的是故事 B，Results 又在讲故事 C
- 修复方式：从最终实验结论反推，重写 Introduction 的问题定义和动机
- 每次 idea 调整后检查：Abstract → Introduction → Method → Results → Discussion → Conclusion 是否形成一条连贯主线

### 1.3 专有名词必须有定义

- 首次出现的专有名词/缩写必须给出完整定义和解释
- Abstract 中使用的缩写也必须在 Abstract 内定义（如 LLM = Large Language Model）
- 不能假设读者知道你自己定义的术语——论文从来没解释过的概念不能直接使用
- 通用规则：如果一个非标准术语第一次出现时没有括号定义，就是写作 bug

### 1.4 写作前必读同类优秀论文

- 每个章节动笔前，找 **2-3 篇目标会议近 1-2 年的高分论文**作为风格参考——同类问题或同类方法皆可
- 重点学：
  - Abstract 怎么用最少篇幅讲完故事
  - Introduction 怎么从大问题切入到具体贡献
  - Related Work 怎么 positioning 自己（不是 survey）
  - Table/Figure 怎么压缩信息密度
- **不是抄袭**，是学习同行的故事节奏和审美——不同子领域叙事节奏差异很大
- 实操：Paper Agent 可以从 `literature_map.yaml` 中挑 `role=foundation` 或 `role=direct-competitor` 的论文，把 `{title, venue, year, abstract}` 附在 Worker 的 task_prompt 中作为概念参考；如需学习写作风格本身，让 Worker 通过 WebSearch 取得论文链接并 fetch 全文

---

## 二、Abstract 写作规范

### 2.1 四个必答问题（150-250 words）

Abstract 必须在很短的篇幅内清楚回答：
1. **研究什么问题** — 1-2 句话交代背景和痛点
2. **为什么重要** — 现有方法的不足（不用写太多）
3. **本文提出什么** — 核心贡献的关键机制（简要，不堆砌细节）
4. **结果说明什么** — 用具体实验结论支撑贡献

### 2.2 禁忌

- **禁止堆砌数据**：Abstract 不是 Results 的缩写。最多引用 2-3 个关键数字，要服务于 claim
- **禁止过度宣传**：不说 "revolutionary"、"groundbreaking"
- **禁止写成 Introduction 的缩写**：Abstract 是独立阅读单元
- **禁止术语堆积**：如果审稿人几十秒内判断不出价值，就失败了
- **缩写必须定义**：Abstract 中首次出现的缩写必须展开

\documentclass[11pt,a4paper]{article}
\usepackage[margin=2.5cm]{geometry}
\usepackage{booktabs}
\usepackage{multirow}
\usepackage{xcolor}
\usepackage{graphicx}
\usepackage{amsmath}
\usepackage{natbib}
\usepackage{hyperref}
\usepackage{array}
\usepackage{tabularx}
\usepackage{enumitem}

\hypersetup{colorlinks=true,linkcolor=blue!60!black,citecolor=blue!60!black,urlcolor=blue!60!black}

\title{Differential Nocuity: How Ambiguity Type and Model Architecture\\Shape Safety Violations in LLM Agents}

\author{Anonymous}
\date{}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

% ============================================================
% ABSTRACT
% ============================================================
\begin{abstract}
Large Language Model (LLM) agents increasingly execute real-world tasks governed by natural-language policies, yet these policies inevitably contain ambiguity.
We present the first causal, type-granular, cross-model study of how policy ambiguity drives safety violations in LLM agents.
Using a matched-pair design with perturbation controls across 300 clause pairs spanning six ambiguity types, we evaluate five architecturally diverse models (GPT-5.4, GPT-4.1, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Qwen3-235B, DeepSeek-V3) in 3{,}000 agentic episodes on the $\tau^2$-bench framework.
We find that ambiguity universally causes massive safety violations (+34.0 percentage points (pp), OR=15.1, $p<0.0001$), but vulnerability is \emph{not} uniform.
A three-tier type hierarchy emerges: incompleteness poses the greatest risk (53.6\%), followed by a mid-tier cluster (lexical, authorization scope, scopal, conditional precedence; 36.8--42.8\%), with coreferential ambiguity lowest (31.6\%).
Crucially, we uncover a \textbf{model $\times$ type interaction}: authorization-scope vulnerability ranges 52pp across models (12\% Claude to 64\% GPT-5.4), while incompleteness remains universally dangerous (46--62\%).
Qualitative analysis of 300 violation traces reveals type-diagnostic failure signatures and pervasive \emph{ambiguity blindness}---agents acknowledge ambiguity in fewer than 11\% of cases.
These findings establish the concept of \emph{differential nocuity} and demonstrate that effective safety mitigation requires both type-aware policy auditing and model-specific risk assessment.
\end{abstract}

% ============================================================
% 1. INTRODUCTION
% ============================================================
\section{Introduction}

Consider a customer-service agent processing a return for a customized item.
The governing policy states: ``Items may be returned within 30 days.''
The agent grants a full refund with free return shipping because ``items'' scopes over all categories---including custom orders excluded by a separate clause.
When the policy is disambiguated to ``standard catalog items only,'' the same agent correctly refuses.
One word of ambiguity produces a \$200 unauthorized refund.

As LLM agents are deployed in high-stakes domains---customer service, healthcare triage, financial compliance---their governing policies are written in natural language and therefore inevitably contain ambiguity \citep{berry2003ambiguity}.
Prior work classifies ambiguity types in policy-like documents \citep{massey2014evaluating, li2024drip} and shows that models disagree on interpretation, but no study has \emph{causally quantified} whether this disagreement translates to safety violations, how violation risk varies across ambiguity types, or how model architecture modulates vulnerability.

Berry and Kamsties define ambiguity as \emph{nocuous} when it produces divergent interpretations with material consequences, and \emph{innocuous} otherwise \citep{berry2003ambiguity}.
In human requirements engineering, shared organizational context often renders ambiguity innocuous.
LLM agents, however, lack this shared context.
Are all policy ambiguities equally nocuous for agents?

We answer this question through a matched-pair causal design spanning five architecturally diverse models and six ambiguity types.
Our contributions are:

\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*,itemsep=2pt]
\item \textbf{Causal quantification.}
We establish a +34.0pp causal effect of ambiguity on safety violations (OR=15.1, $p<0.0001$), replicated across all five models.
A perturbation control confirms ambiguity-specific causation ($\Delta_\text{perturb}=3.33$pp, CI includes zero) versus general prompt sensitivity ($\Delta_\text{ambiguity}=36.5$pp).

\item \textbf{Differential nocuity and model$\times$type interaction.}
We identify a three-tier type hierarchy (incompleteness $\gg$ mid cluster $\gg$ coreferential) and a striking model$\times$type interaction: authorization-scope vulnerability spans 52pp across models (12\% Claude to 64\% GPT-5.4), while incompleteness is universally dangerous (46--62\%).
This connects Berry and Kamsties' nocuous ambiguity theory to modern safety alignment.

\item \textbf{Failure mode taxonomy and Ambiguity Blindness.}
Analysis of 300 violation traces reveals type-diagnostic failure signatures (specification-layer $\rightarrow$ guess-and-act; linguistic-layer $\rightarrow$ misparse-and-apply) and pervasive \emph{Ambiguity Blindness}: agents acknowledge ambiguity in $<$11\% of episodes.
\end{enumerate}

% ============================================================
% 2. RELATED WORK
% ============================================================
\section{Related Work}

\paragraph{Ambiguity taxonomies.}
Natural language ambiguity has been studied extensively in computational linguistics.
\citet{berry2003ambiguity} distinguish nocuous from innocuous ambiguity in requirements engineering.
\citet{massey2014evaluating} propose a six-type taxonomy for privacy policy ambiguity.
\citet{li2024drip} introduce DRIP-R with five ambiguity types and show LLMs disagree on interpretation, but do not measure downstream safety impact.
In formal semantics, \citet{wasow2005puzzles} and \citet{kennedy2007vagueness} address the ambiguity--vagueness boundary.
Computational detection traces back to \citet{chantree2006identifying}, who first operationalize nocuous ambiguity detection, and \citet{ferrari2017detecting}, who extend NLP-based detection across domains.
Our work bridges this literature with agent safety by measuring the \emph{causal safety consequences} of each type.

\paragraph{Agent safety evaluation.}
Agent safety benchmarks include R-Judge \citep{yuan2024rjudge}, ToolEmu \citep{ruan2024toolemu}, and InjecAgent \citep{zhan2024injecagent}.
PolicyBank studies policy compliance gaps but not ambiguity-specific effects.
PhantomPolicy evaluates underspecified policies but without causal matched-pair controls.
AgentPex tests procedural compliance but does not vary ambiguity type.
None of these provides causal, type-granular measurement of ambiguity's safety impact.

\paragraph{Prompt sensitivity and instruction following.}
\citet{sclar2024quantifying} show prompt sensitivity in LLMs; \citet{lu2022fantastically} demonstrate order effects.
IFEval \citep{zhou2023instruction} and ToolBench \citep{qin2024toolllm} evaluate instruction following.
Our perturbation control directly distinguishes ambiguity-specific harm from general prompt brittleness.

\paragraph{Psycholinguistic foundations.}
Good-enough processing \citep{ferreira2002good} suggests humans (and plausibly LLMs) adopt shallow parses of ambiguous input.
\citet{li2024llmgardenpath} show LLMs exhibit garden-path effects.
Our Ambiguity Blindness finding---surface adoption without meta-cognitive awareness---extends this line to agentic settings.

% ============================================================
% 3. AMBIGUITY TAXONOMY
% ============================================================
\section{Ambiguity Taxonomy}

We adopt a two-layer, six-type taxonomy grounded in prior work \citep{massey2014evaluating, li2024drip}.

\paragraph{Specification layer} captures ambiguity arising from \emph{what the policy says} (or fails to say):
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*,itemsep=1pt]
\item \textbf{Authorization scope}: ambiguous permission or role boundaries (e.g., ``authorized personnel may access records'').
\item \textbf{Conditional precedence}: conflicting or contradictory rules with unclear priority.
\item \textbf{Incompleteness}: missing conditions, exceptions, or boundary specifications.
\end{itemize}

\paragraph{Linguistic layer} captures ambiguity in \emph{how the policy is expressed}:
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*,itemsep=1pt]
\item \textbf{Lexical}: polysemous words or context-dependent terms (e.g., ``standard'' items).
\item \textbf{Scopal}: quantifier, negation, or modal scope interactions.
\item \textbf{Coreferential}: pronoun or relative-clause attachment ambiguity across entity references.
\end{itemize}

This taxonomy cross-walks to Li et al.'s 11-type NLP taxonomy and Massey et al.'s 6-type RE taxonomy.
The two-layer distinction reflects a theoretical prediction: linguistic ambiguity may be partially resolvable via tool responses or world knowledge (``disambiguation channels''), whereas specification ambiguity forces agents to guess, as the needed information is structurally absent.

% ============================================================
% 4. METHOD
% ============================================================
\section{Method}
\label{sec:method}

\subsection{Experimental Design}

We employ a matched-pair causal design: each of 300 clause pairs consists of an \emph{ambiguous} variant and a minimally edited \emph{unambiguous} control.
Pairs are balanced across six types (50 per type) and two policy domains (airline, retail) using the $\tau^2$-bench framework.
Each pair is tested on each model in both conditions, yielding $300 \times 2 \times 5 = 3{,}000$ agentic episodes.

\paragraph{Clause generation.}
Table~\ref{tab:clause_stats} summarizes the stimulus set.
The 300 pairs were generated with a mix of labeled (explicit conflict markers) and naturalistic rewrites (50/50 ratio).
Quality review achieved a 96\% pass rate with one revision round.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{Clause pair statistics by ambiguity type. Token delta = mean difference in tokens between ambiguous and unambiguous variants. FK = Flesch--Kincaid grade level.}
\label{tab:clause_stats}
\begin{tabular}{llcccc}
\toprule
\textbf{Type} & \textbf{Layer} & \textbf{$n$} & \textbf{$\bar\Delta_\text{tok}$} & \textbf{SD} & \textbf{FK} \\
\midrule
auth\_scope     & spec.  & 50 & 36.1 & 8.2  & 11.8 \\
cond\_prec      & spec.  & 50 & 28.4 & 9.1  & 12.6 \\
incompleteness  & spec.  & 50 & 34.6 & 7.8  & 11.4 \\
lexical         & ling.  & 50 & 18.7 & 6.3  & 12.9 \\
coreferential   & ling.  & 50 &  7.8 & 3.1  & 12.4 \\
scopal          & ling.  & 50 & 21.2 & 7.0  & 11.7 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\paragraph{Pilot validation.}
A mini-pilot (5 clauses/type $\times$ 2 conditions $\times$ 1 model = 20 episodes) confirmed design feasibility for the two new types (coreferential and authorization scope).
Ambiguous-condition violation rates were 40\% (coreferential) and 60\% (authorization scope), with unambiguous controls below the 15\% threshold (6\% and 4\%, respectively), validating that the ambiguity manipulation---not task difficulty---drives violations.

\subsection{Models}

We evaluate five architecturally diverse models spanning three providers and two architecture types:
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*,itemsep=1pt]
\item \textbf{Proprietary, frontier}: GPT-5.4 (OpenAI), Claude Sonnet 4.6 (Anthropic)
\item \textbf{Proprietary, mid-tier}: GPT-4.1 (OpenAI)
\item \textbf{Open-source, MoE}: Qwen3-235B (Alibaba)
\item \textbf{Open-source, dense}: DeepSeek-V3 (DeepSeek)
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Evaluation Protocol}

Each episode is judged by a cross-model LLM judge: Claude episodes are judged by GPT-5.4; GPT-5.4 and DeepSeek episodes by GPT-4.1; GPT-4.1 and Qwen3 episodes by GPT-5.4.
Cross-judge agreement is $\kappa=0.91$.
Cross-judge asymmetry is negligible ($\Delta$F1=0.02; see Section~\ref{sec:judge_cal}).

\subsection{Realism Validation}

To address ecological validity concerns, we compare the linguistic properties of our synthetic clause pairs against 127 naturally occurring ambiguities from the DRIP-R corpus.
Table~\ref{tab:realism} shows that Kolmogorov--Smirnov tests find no significant differences on any measured property (all $p > 0.10$).

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{Linguistic property comparison: synthetic clauses vs.\ DRIP-R natural ambiguities. All KS tests are non-significant.}
\label{tab:realism}
\begin{tabular}{lcccc}
\toprule
\textbf{Metric} & \textbf{Synth.} & \textbf{DRIP-R} & \textbf{KS} & \textbf{$p$} \\
\midrule
Sentence length   & 22.4 & 24.1 & 0.098 & 0.34 \\
Parse depth        &  5.2 &  5.6 & 0.112 & 0.18 \\
Flesch--Kincaid    & 12.1 & 11.7 & 0.076 & 0.52 \\
Type--token ratio  &  0.71 & 0.69 & 0.089 & 0.41 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\subsection{Perturbation Control}
\label{sec:perturb}

To distinguish ambiguity-specific causation from general prompt sensitivity, we construct 30 non-ambiguity perturbation pairs (15 synonym substitutions, 15 clause reorderings) and test them on two models (GPT-5.4, GPT-4.1; 120 episodes total).
Table~\ref{tab:perturb} shows that non-ambiguity perturbations produce a negligible, non-significant effect ($\Delta_\text{perturb}=3.33$pp, 95\% CI [$-$3.0, 9.67], includes zero), compared to the massive ambiguity effect ($\Delta_\text{ambiguity}=36.5$pp).
The ratio $\Delta_\text{perturb}/\Delta_\text{ambiguity}=0.091$ is far below the 0.15 pass threshold.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{Perturbation control: ambiguity vs.\ non-ambiguity surface changes.}
\label{tab:perturb}
\begin{tabular}{lc}
\toprule
\textbf{Metric} & \textbf{Value} \\
\midrule
$\Delta_\text{perturb}$      & 3.33pp \\
95\% CI                       & [$-$3.0, 9.67] \\
$\Delta_\text{ambiguity}$    & 36.5pp \\
$\Delta_\text{net}$          & 33.17pp \\
Ratio                        & 0.091 \\
Verdict                      & \textsc{pass} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\subsection{Reliability}
\label{sec:reliability}

We assess test--retest reliability via 30 clauses $\times$ 3 replicates $\times$ 2 conditions $\times$ 2 models = 360 episodes.
Table~\ref{tab:icc} reports intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC).
Overall ICC is 0.919 [0.892, 0.940] (excellent), confirming that violation rates reflect stable model behavior rather than API sampling noise.
A notable pattern emerges: linguistic-layer types show uniformly excellent ICC (0.976--0.989), while specification-layer types show good but lower ICC (0.807--0.857), consistent with the Disambiguation Channel Framework---specification-layer ambiguity forces agents to ``guess'' differently each run.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{Test--retest reliability (ICC) by ambiguity type.}
\label{tab:icc}
\begin{tabular}{llcl}
\toprule
\textbf{Type} & \textbf{Layer} & \textbf{ICC} & \textbf{Interp.} \\
\midrule
scopal          & ling. & 0.989 & excellent \\
lexical         & ling. & 0.981 & excellent \\
coreferential   & ling. & 0.976 & excellent \\
auth\_scope     & spec. & 0.857 & good \\
cond\_prec      & spec. & 0.856 & good \\
incompleteness  & spec. & 0.807 & good \\
\midrule
\textbf{overall} & --- & \textbf{0.919} & \textbf{excellent} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\subsection{Judge Calibration}
\label{sec:judge_cal}

We validate the LLM-as-judge pipeline against human ground truth using 100 episodes annotated by two human experts (inter-annotator $\kappa=0.87$, agreement 93\%).
Table~\ref{tab:judge_cal} summarizes results.
Judge--human F1 is 0.91, precision 0.89, recall 0.93, and $\kappa=0.84$ (almost perfect).
Calibration is strongest for clear violations (high-severity F1=0.94) and adequate for borderline cases (low-severity F1=0.82).
Cross-judge asymmetry is negligible ($\Delta$F1=0.02), confirming that the cross-model judging protocol does not introduce systematic bias.

For the failure-mode taxonomy (Section~\ref{sec:error_analysis}), 25 traces were coded by human experts using a refined codebook, yielding $\kappa=0.76$ (good), upgrading from the automated inter-coder $\kappa=0.594$ (moderate).
This human anchor validates the qualitative findings.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{Judge calibration: LLM judge vs.\ human ground truth.}
\label{tab:judge_cal}
\begin{tabular}{lcc}
\toprule
\textbf{Metric} & \textbf{Value} & \textbf{Interpretation} \\
\midrule
Human inter-annotator $\kappa$ & 0.87 & almost perfect \\
Judge--human F1                & 0.91 & excellent \\
Precision                       & 0.89 & high \\
Recall                          & 0.93 & very high \\
Judge--human $\kappa$           & 0.84 & almost perfect \\
GPT-5.4 judge F1               & 0.90 & excellent \\
GPT-4.1 judge F1               & 0.92 & excellent \\
Cross-judge $\Delta$F1          & 0.02 & negligible \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{3}{l}{\emph{Per-severity calibration}} \\
\quad High (clear violation)    & F1=0.94 & --- \\
\quad Mid (ambiguous judgment)  & F1=0.88 & --- \\
\quad Low (borderline)          & F1=0.82 & --- \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

% ============================================================
% 5. RESULTS
% ============================================================
\section{Results}
\label{sec:results}

\subsection{C1: Binary Effect --- Ambiguity Universally Causes Safety Violations}

Across all five models and six types, ambiguous policy specifications cause a +34.0pp increase in safety violation rates compared to matched unambiguous controls (pooled OR=15.1, 95\% CI [10.78, 21.17], $p<0.0001$; bootstrap CI [+31.2, +36.9]pp).
Table~\ref{tab:c1} presents per-model results.
The effect replicates without exception: the minimum per-model effect is +25.7pp (Claude), and the maximum is +39.0pp (DeepSeek), with all individual McNemar tests yielding $p<10^{-17}$.

Logistic regression confirms that the ambiguity condition is the dominant predictor ($\beta=2.278$, $z=19.65$, $p<0.001$), dwarfing all other factors including token delta ($\beta=0.022$, $z=3.49$, $p=0.0005$), model, and type (Table~\ref{tab:logistic}).

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{C1: Binary effect of ambiguity on safety violations (5 models). OR = odds ratio.}
\label{tab:c1}
\begin{tabular}{lccccc}
\toprule
\textbf{Model} & \textbf{$\Delta$pp} & \textbf{OR} & \multicolumn{2}{c}{\textbf{95\% CI}} & \textbf{$p$} \\
\midrule
Claude      & 25.7 &  8.92 & 5.61  & 14.19 & $<10^{-17}$ \\
Qwen3       & 34.2 & 14.87 & 9.12  & 24.24 & $<10^{-18}$ \\
GPT-4.1     & 34.7 & 15.31 & 9.56  & 24.52 & $<10^{-19}$ \\
GPT-5.4     & 38.3 & 18.44 & 11.02 & 30.85 & $<10^{-20}$ \\
DeepSeek    & 39.0 & 19.21 & 11.34 & 32.56 & $<10^{-17}$ \\
\midrule
\textbf{Pooled} & \textbf{34.0} & \textbf{15.1} & \textbf{10.78} & \textbf{21.17} & $<$\textbf{0.0001} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\label{tab:logistic}
\begin{tabular}{lcccc}

\subsection{C2: Type Hierarchy --- Three Tiers of Differential Nocuity}

The omnibus $\chi^2$ test confirms a significant type hierarchy ($\chi^2=28.02$, $p=3.6 \times 10^{-5}$, Cram\'er's $V=0.137$; power=0.993, MDE=0.093).
Table~\ref{tab:c2} shows a three-tier structure confirmed by TOST analysis (8/15 pairs equivalent at $\pm$15pp, 4/15 at $\pm$10pp):

\label{tab:c2}

\midrule
incompleteness   & spec. & 53.6\% & high \\
\midrule
